nodes.label: faq.md
nodes.rationale: We believe that reservoir simulation should be a library and not necessarily an application by itself. The future of porous media simulation is deeply integrated into other workflows, and not as an application that simply writes files to disk. As a part of experimentation in differentiable and flexible solvers using automatic differentiation that started with MRST, Julia was the natural next step.

nodes.label: Newton's method
nodes.rationale: JutulDarcy solves systems that generally have both non-smooth behavior and physical constraints on the values. For that reason, Newton's method is modified to limit updates (Appleyard chopping, pressure/saturation/composition limits) so variables stay within physical boundaries.

nodes.label: Block Backend
nodes.rationale: Determines the matrix format (block-CSC using StaticArrays.jl) and consequently the linear solver type to be used, enabling much more efficient sparse matrix-vector products and standard preconditioners.

nodes.label: CPRPreconditioner
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage physics-informed preconditioner that seeks to decouple the global pressure part of the system from the local transport part, applying AMG to the pressure equation and ILU(0) to the full system.

nodes.label: Schur Complement
nodes.rationale: Explicitly forming the Schur complement matrix J_rr - J_rw J_ww^-1 J_wr will lead to a lot of fill-in. JutulDarcy instead uses its action as a linear operator from LinearOperators.jl, applying the inverse of the well system when computing the residual/action. This is inexpensive because J_ww is small and the factorization can be stored.

nodes.label: Viscous Fingering Representation
nodes.rationale: The wavy green-to-blue interface represents viscous fingering, which is a classic Saffman-Taylor instability in porous media and reservoir simulation.

nodes.label: Darcy Symbol Design
nodes.rationale: The stylized lowercase 'd' or partial derivative symbol '∂' in the center represents both Darcy's law and partial differential equations governing flow in porous media.

nodes.label: Julia Colors Integration
nodes.rationale: The logo uses the Red, Green, Blue, and Purple colors of the Julia programming language to denote that the package is written in Julia.
